organization.name: Fresh Start Community Services, Incorporated
organization.mission: The purpose of Fresh Start Community Services, Incorporated is to provide an array of services that make a difference in the lives of our youth, young adults, women, men, senior citizens, disenfranchised individuals, and the indigenous in the community who choose to receive our support in allowing us to play an active role in their lives and getting to know their interests and their passions. We work together to identify the services that focus on developing healthy relationships, support individual decisions and provide instruction and services in a safe environment. Inspirational services will also be provided for individuals. These goals are accomplished with love, compassion, integrity, and without judgement.
organization.vision: Our vision is to enhance the cultural and community development in disenfranchised communities by giving individuals the opportunity to develop new skills, receive case management support, job training and networking in a welcoming environment. Individuals will have the opportunity to integrate into the larger American society by interacting and sharing their cultures and skills in our organization.

pages.hero_headline: Hope, Dignity, and Real Opportunities for Every Community Member
pages.hero_subheadline: Providing an array of transformative services that empower youth, seniors, families, and disenfranchised individuals with compassion, integrity, and without judgement.

leadership.name: Rev. Dr. Marcus A. Vance
leadership.title: Executive Director & Founder
leadership.bio_short: Over two decades of servant leadership, community mobilization, and dedication to uplifting families and disenfranchised populations.
leadership.bio_full: Rev. Dr. Marcus A. Vance brings over twenty years of community pastoral leadership, non-profit governance, and social service innovation to Fresh Start Community Services, Inc. Under his guidance, FSC has expanded from neighborhood outreach to a comprehensive community support ecosystem encompassing food security, career workshops, and restorative programs. He holds advanced degrees in Community Development and Pastoral Care, focusing on holistic healing without judgement.
leadership.credentials: D.Min., M.Div., Certified Community Outreach Director

leadership.name: Eleanor Sterling, MSW
leadership.title: Board President & Director of Family Services
leadership.bio_short: Licensed clinical social worker with a passionate focus on family stability, senior care, and trauma-informed community support.
leadership.bio_full: Eleanor Sterling has dedicated 18 years to family advocacy, child welfare, and community mental health programs. As Board President of FSC, she ensures all program curricula maintain trauma-informed standards, cultural sensitivity, and ethical accountability. Eleanor frequently conducts the Safer Home Life and Beginning the Journey self-awareness workshops.

leadership.name: Carlos Mendoza, MBA
leadership.title: Treasurer & Workforce Development Lead
leadership.bio_short: Finance and workforce transition specialist mentoring youth and adults in financial literacy and employment readiness.
leadership.bio_full: Carlos Mendoza leads the financial stewardship and career training tracks at Fresh Start Community Services. He brings senior corporate finance experience and a heartfelt mission to eliminate barriers for job seekers, formerly incarcerated individuals, and unhoused neighbors. Carlos oversees the Getting Ready for Success! workshop series.

leadership.name: Tamara Jenkins
leadership.title: Director of Pantry & Community Care
leadership.bio_short: Organizer of the Circle of Love Food & Clothing Pantry, coordinating weekly distributions and compassionate neighbor-to-neighbor aid.
leadership.bio_full: Tamara Jenkins coordinates regional food supply logistics, warehouse operations, clothing drives, and community volunteers for the Circle of Love Food & Clothing Pantry. Her deep community ties ensure thousands of families receive healthy food, warm winter coats, and personal care necessities every season.
leadership.credentials: Certified Food Safety Manager, Community Organizer

programs.title: Getting Ready for Success! Workshops
programs.description_short: Career readiness, resume tailoring, mock interviewing, and workplace etiquette in an empowering environment.
programs.description_full: The Getting Ready for Success! Workshops guide participants through every step of job placement and personal professional growth. Through hands-on practice, attendees build tailored resumes, practice interview techniques, receive interview-ready attire through our partner network, and develop critical communication habits for long-term workplace retention.
programs.target_population: Youth, young adults, re-entering citizens, and job seekers

programs.title: Self-Awareness Workshops ("Beginning the Journey")
programs.description_short: A transformative curriculum helping individuals identify core strengths, process life transitions, and discover purpose.
programs.description_full: Beginning the Journey is a structured self-awareness series created to give individuals space to examine personal choices, unpack past challenges, and chart healthy forward pathways. Guided by compassionate facilitators, participants explore emotional triggers, boundary-setting, and positive relationship dynamics.
programs.target_population: Individuals experiencing life transitions, stress, or recovery

programs.title: Images of You (Self-Confidence Workshops)
programs.description_short: Cultivating internal worth, dignified self-presentation, and interpersonal poise for women, men, and youth.
programs.description_full: Images of You focuses on self-image, public speaking, grooming, positive self-talk, and overcoming self-doubt. Participants discover that self-confidence is a skill that can be nurtured, enabling them to pursue education, employment, and social engagement with heads held high.
programs.target_population: Women, men, and youth seeking renewed self-esteem

programs.title: Circle of Love Food & Clothing Pantry
programs.description_short: Weekly distributions of fresh groceries, pantry staples, seasonal apparel, and personal hygiene essentials.
programs.description_full: The Circle of Love Food & Clothing Pantry is the emergency safety net of Fresh Start Community Services. Open weekly, the pantry serves hundreds of families with dignity and warmth. No one in need is turned away. We partner with regional food banks, local farms, and community drives to supply nutritious meals and weather-appropriate clothing.
programs.target_population: Under-resourced families, children, seniors, and unhoused neighbors

programs.title: Financial Planning & Budgeting Workshops
programs.description_short: Actionable guidance on budgeting, checking accounts, credit building, and eliminating debt cycles.
programs.description_full: Understanding finances is key to breaking systemic poverty. Our Financial Planning/Budgeting Workshops demystify banking, credit scores, emergency savings, and debt avoidance. Participants leave with an individualized monthly household budget and one-on-one financial coaching support.
programs.target_population: Working families, young adults, and individuals rebuilding credit

programs.title: Senior Citizen Program
programs.description_short: Wellness check-ins, nutritious food delivery, digital literacy classes, and fellowship for older adults.
programs.description_full: Our seniors are cherished pillars of our community. The FSC Senior Citizen Program prevents social isolation through telephone wellness check-ins, home delivery of pantry goods for homebound elders, social luncheons, and digital literacy support to help seniors connect with grandchildren and telehealth doctors.
programs.target_population: Seniors aged 60+, retired community members, and caregivers

programs.title: Disenfranchised / Indigenous Care Program
programs.description_short: Culturally attuned outreach, case navigation, resource sharing, and community partnership advocacy.
programs.description_full: Dedicated to honoring heritage while addressing systemic inequities, this program bridges vital healthcare, housing, and social services with Indigenous traditions and disenfranchised neighborhood networks. We listen first, partnering with tribal and community representatives to deliver responsive, respectful support.
programs.target_population: Indigenous community members, disenfranchised households, and underserved groups

programs.title: Fresh Anointing Shiloh Inspirational Services
programs.description_short: Non-judgmental spiritual encouragement, compassionate prayer, and community uplift for weary hearts.
programs.description_full: Recognizing that emotional and spiritual well-being are foundational to whole-person restoration, Fresh Anointing Shiloh provides weekly gatherings of inspiration, encouragement, music, and hope. All community members are embraced with open arms regardless of background or past mistakes.
programs.target_population: Anyone seeking spiritual comfort, hope, and community fellowship

programs.title: Safer Home Life Environment Workshops
programs.description_short: Equipping households with communication tools, conflict de-escalation, and safety planning for resilient families.
programs.description_full: Healthy families build vibrant neighborhoods. These workshops offer parents, partners, and extended family members practical approaches to de-escalate tension, establish consistent routines for children, and create a physically and emotionally secure sanctuary in the home.
programs.target_population: Parents, guardians, couples, and multi-generational households

programs.title: Civic Responsibility Workshops
programs.description_short: Empowering residents with community organizing skills, voting awareness, and neighborhood stewardship.
programs.description_full: Civic Responsibility Workshops inspire participants to see themselves as active stakeholders and changemakers. Topics include understanding local municipal governance, neighborhood council participation, community clean-ups, and constructive community advocacy.
programs.target_population: Young adults, neighborhood residents, and emerging community organizers

programs.title: Youth & Young Adult Empowerment Initiative
programs.description_short: One-on-one mentorship, creative workshops, college readiness, and leadership retreats for teens and young adults.
programs.description_full: Our youth initiative pairs youth ages 13 to 24 with dedicated community mentors who provide steady guidance, homework assistance, leadership training, and safe weekend social activities. We believe in investing deeply in the passions of young people.
programs.target_population: Youth and young adults ages 13 to 24

programs.title: Community Cultural Development & Networking
programs.description_short: Celebrating diverse heritage through community showcases, shared skill workshops, and cross-cultural dialogue.
programs.description_full: Fulfilling our vision to integrate and celebrate cultures, this initiative hosts monthly cultural food and story exchanges, artisan markets, and networking forums where community members teach each other their traditions and skills.
programs.target_population: Multicultural community members, immigrants, and neighborhood residents

programs.title: Case Management & Job Training Transition Program
programs.description_short: Individualized case plans, vocational training connections, childcare coordination, and post-placement support.
programs.description_full: A comprehensive wraparound program pairing participants with a dedicated case manager. We assess individual barriers to stability, connect clients with accredited vocational apprenticeships, and provide ongoing check-ins for 12 months after placement.
programs.target_population: Adults seeking sustainable employment, career transitions, and life stability

articles.title: Circle of Love Pantry Expands Winter Distribution Schedule
articles.excerpt: To meet rising community needs during colder months, FSC is extending pantry operating hours and adding a Saturday hot breakfast service.
articles.content:
Fresh Start Community Services is pleased to announce an expansion of our **Circle of Love Food & Clothing Pantry** operating schedule beginning this winter season.

Thanks to the generous dedication of our volunteer teams and our network of food donors, the pantry will now welcome community members:
- **Tuesdays & Thursdays:** 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM
- **Saturdays:** 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM (including fresh produce and hot morning meal service)

### Serving Without Stigma
"Every person who walks through our doors is family," shares Tamara Jenkins, Director of Pantry Services. "Our commitment has always been clear: no judgment, no unnecessary hurdles, just warm encouragement and healthy nourishment."

Families can receive canned protein, fresh dairy, vegetables, diapers, and winter warm coats for children. If you would like to volunteer or coordinate a food drive, please visit our Get Involved page or contact us today.

articles.title: Celebrating 24 New Graduates of Getting Ready for Success!
articles.excerpt: Our latest workshop cohort concluded with a celebration of perseverance, updated career portfolios, and 18 immediate job interview placements.
articles.content:
We celebrated a momentous milestone this past Friday as 24 dedicated individuals completed our six-week **Getting Ready for Success!** career readiness curriculum.

Over six intensive workshop sessions, participants:
1. Revamped their resumes to highlight transferable life experiences.
2. Practiced mock panel interviews with local business leaders.
3. Prepared personal elevator pitches and learned conflict management strategies.
4. Received a professional wardrobe bundle tailored for their industry targets.

Eighteen participants have already scheduled first-round interviews with our corporate and nonprofit employment partners. Congratulations to our cohort on this courageous new beginning!

articles.title: Indigenous Care Initiative Announces New Community Health Circles
articles.excerpt: Strengthening cultural ties and accessible healthcare pathways through collaborative community sharing circles.
articles.content:
In alignment with our founding vision to enhance cultural and community development, FSC is launching monthly Community Health & Tradition Circles in partnership with regional Indigenous elders and advocates.

These gatherings will provide safe, culturally resonant spaces to discuss holistic wellness, elder support, youth cultural continuity, and mutual aid. All community members are invited to join in mutual respect and active listening.
